state:
- The central target, Nup98, is not anchored in any supplied evidence: the packet only says 'nuclear-pore and transport components' associate with TDP-43, so choosing Nup98 over other FG-nucleoporins (Nup153, Nup214, Nup62) is a bare assumption even though the hypothesis frames itself as evidence-driven. Fix: either justify Nup98 by citing whether the S1 pore proteomics flagged it, or convert arm (a) into an unbiased phospho-screen across multiple FG-nucleoporins in stressed motor_neurons and let the phosphorylation pattern pick the candidate before committing to knock-ins.
- The upstream kinase is left as a disjunction (p38 MAPK OR JNK), which weakens the causal claim and makes the phospho-null prediction ambiguous, since S/TP sites are shared by both proline-directed kinases. Fix: add a kinase-discrimination arm using selective inhibitors or CRISPR/epistasis (e.g., p38 vs JNK inhibition with phosphorylation-site resolution) so that 'stress-activated phosphorylation' becomes one defined kinase, not a class.
- The biophysical bridge (phosphorylation weakens FG-network cohesion enough to slow physiological import) has no quantitative precedent in or outside the packet and is only asserted; it could fail because interphase Nup98 phosphorylation stoichiometry in neurons is low or because redundant FG-nups buffer the barrier. Fix: include a minimal in vitro test — purified Nup98 GLFG domain phosphorylated by the candidate kinase versus the S/T-to-A variant, measuring FG phase separation or reconstituted-pore permeability — to validate the mechanism before interpreting iPSC-neuron rescue as proof.
